props.gloss_en: R' Yehuda (mishna): the prohibition of the sciatic nerve applies even to a non-kosher animal
R' Yehuda (mishna): was the sciatic nerve not forbidden from the sons of Jacob, while a non-kosher animal was still permitted to them?

R' Yehuda (baraita): the carcass of a non-kosher bird does not defile garments in the throat -- 'a carcass or torn he shall not eat to defile himself with it' (Lev 22:8) covers one whose ban is 'do not eat a carcass', excluding this one whose ban is 'do not eat a non-kosher one'
and if you say: he holds sinews do not impart flavour, so in a non-kosher animal there is the nerve's prohibition, and the non-kosher prohibition is absent
R' Yehuda (baraita): one who eats the sciatic nerve of a non-kosher animal is liable twice
R' Shimon (baraita): he is exempt
actually, he holds sinews impart flavour
and he holds [the nerve's prohibition] applies to a fetus
so the nerve's prohibition and the non-kosher prohibition arrive together
the mishna (89b): R' Yehuda: it does not apply to a fetus, and its fat is permitted
that [R' Yehuda's exemption of the fetus] is said of a kosher animal
for the Merciful One said: 'every [one] among the animals you may eat' (Deut 14:6)
but in a non-kosher animal it applies [to the fetus]
the mishna (Nazir): for these impurities a nazirite shaves -- for a corpse and for an olive-bulk of a corpse
R' Yochanan: ['for a corpse'] is needed only for a miscarried fetus whose limbs were not yet joined by sinews
evidently the non-kosher prohibition ('issur tumah') comes first
even though the non-kosher prohibition comes first, the nerve's prohibition comes and takes effect on it, since its prohibition applies to the sons of Noach
Rava: actually [R' Shimon] holds sinews do not impart flavour

Rava: and there it is different, for the verse says 'therefore the sons of Israel shall not eat the sciatic nerve' (Gen 32:33) -- one whose nerve is forbidden and meat permitted, excluding this one whose nerve and meat are both forbidden
R' Meir: one who eats the sciatic nerve of a carcass is liable twice
the Sages: he is liable only once
and the Sages concede to R' Meir that one who eats the sciatic nerve of a burnt-offering or of a stoned ox is liable twice
this tanna does not hold that an inclusive prohibition takes effect on a prohibition
but he does hold that a prohibition that is inclusive and graver takes effect
Rava: it is R' Yosei HaGelili
the mishna (Zevachim): an impure man who ate sacred food, whether impure or pure sacred food, is liable
R' Yosei HaGelili: an impure man who ate pure [sacred food] is liable
R' Yosei HaGelili: an impure man who ate impure [sacred food] is exempt, for he ate only an impure thing
they said to him: even an impure man who ate the pure -- once he touched it, he made it impure
Rava: where the body became impure and then the meat -- all agree he is liable, for the karet prohibition came first
Rava: they dispute where the meat became impure and then the body
an inclusive prohibition takes effect on a prohibition: since he is liable for pure pieces generally, he is liable for an impure piece too
Rava: R' Yosei HaGelili does not hold an inclusive prohibition [takes effect]; we do not say 'since'
Rav Ashi: who tells us body impurity is the graver? perhaps meat impurity is graver, since it has no purification in a mikveh
Shabbat and Yom Kippur [together]: one who unwittingly did labour is liable for each by itself -- 'it is Shabbat', 'it is Yom Kippur'
he is liable only once
R' Yosei b'R' Chanina (sent by Ravin): so is the presentation of the teaching, but reverse [the attributions]
R' Yochanan: per R' Yosei HaGelili as we reversed it -- unwitting as to Shabbat, deliberate as to Yom Kippur: liable
R' Yochanan: deliberate as to Shabbat, unwitting as to Yom Kippur: exempt
Abaye: Shabbat is fixed and established; Yom Kippur -- it is the court that fixes it
Rava: rather, it was a persecution, and they sent from there that Yom Kippur of this year is on Shabbat
